name: Bladder cancer
theme: the intravesical era · the EV+P rewrite

meta.title: Bladder cancer in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Urothelial carcinoma of the bladder (NMIBC, MIBC, metastatic), adult
meta.population: Adults with urothelial carcinoma, bladder-centric with upper-tract disease noted inside (same systemic drugs; nephroureterectomy replaces cystectomy - NCCN itself covers upper-tract tumors inside the bladder guideline). Variant histologies (squamous, adenocarcinoma including urachal) ride as notes; small-cell/neuroendocrine bladder cancer is different biology on small-cell principles (neoadjuvant etoposide-platinum, the tempo the sclc trainer teaches) and reroutes. The main axis is depth: non-muscle-invasive (the recurrence-heavy surveillance disease and the intravesical era), muscle-invasive (the perioperative question, rewritten twice in eighteen months), and metastatic (the EV+P rewrite - the trainer whose 1L card carries the registry's earlier impostor-PMID trap, re-checked and re-passed this sweep).
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the disease the last two years rewrote at every depth. NMIBC: BCG for the naive (under a still-current shortage, named), and for BCG-unresponsive CIS a four-option modern set rendered with the maturity discipline intact - pembrolizumab (CR 41%), nadofaragene (53.4%), Anktiva + BCG (71% trial / 62% label), and INLEXZO/TAR-200 (approved 2025-09, CR 82.4%) - all COMPLETE-RESPONSE evidence that displays labeled and never ranks, beside the radical-cystectomy card that owns the survival number. MIBC: the perioperative story rewritten twice - NIAGARA's durval…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: AJCC TNM with the NMIBC/MIBC depth line (T1 vs T2) as the operative fork; NMIBC risk stratification per guideline (secondhand - 403); Galsky consensus criteria define cisplatin eligibility (any one: ECOG >=2, CrCl <60, grade >=2 hearing loss or neuropathy, NYHA >=III)
meta.response: RECIST 1.1 for metastatic disease; for BCG-unresponsive CIS the load-bearing read is complete response at 3-6 months - a response category the FDA itself licenses against; cystoscopic surveillance is NMIBC's standing read

Disease.label: Histology
Disease.help: Small-cell bladder cancer is treated on small-cell principles (neoadjuvant etoposide-platinum, fast tempo - the discipline the sclc trainer teaches); pure variant histologies get their guideline sect…

Disease.label: Depth (the fork)
Disease.help: The T1-vs-T2 muscle line is the fork everything hangs on - and it is only as good as the TURBT that read it (muscle in the specimen, or re-resect). The three menus share almost nothing.
Disease.helpPatient: How deep the tumor goes into the bladder wall decides which of three very different plans applies - and the biopsy has to be deep enough to answer honestly.

NMIBC routing.label: BCG status (NMIBC routing)
NMIBC routing.help: BCG-unresponsive is a formal FDA-defined category, and its modern menu is four options deep (pembrolizumab, nadofaragene, Anktiva, INLEXZO) - all licensed against complete-response evidence, which is…
NMIBC routing.helpPatient: Whether the standard bladder immunotherapy already failed decides between the newer bladder-sparing options and the definitive operation.

Fitness routing.helpPatient: A five-item fitness checklist decides whether the strongest chemotherapy drug is safe - and the newest treatments often work around it entirely.

Newly diagnosed.name: TURBT + intravesical BCG (the standard, under a named shortage)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN NMIBC framework (secondhand - 403); BCG shortage current (allocation)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: guideline standard on decades of randomized intravesical evidence (framing); survival figure flagged
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: BCG cystitis is expected and managed; BCGosis is the rare emergency (anti-TB therapy); the deeper cost is the surveillance calendar itself
Newly diagnosed.patient: For shallow tumors: scrape the tumor out completely, then a course of immune-stimulating bladder instillations - survival is excellent; the real work is the camera-check calendar, because these tumors like to come back shallow.
drugs: TURBT + intravesical BCG (gem/doce where shortage bites)

Newly diagnosed.name: BCG-unresponsive bladder-sparing set (the four modern options - CR-grade, labeled)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: four FDA approvals (pembro 2020-01, nadofaragene 2022-12, Anktiva 2024-04-22, INLEXZO 2025-09-09 - dates secondhand except as flagged); the…
Newly diagnosed.evidence: single-arm CR-rate cohorts (KEYNOTE-057 / NCT02773849 / QUILT-3.032 / SunRISe-1) - labeled, never ranked
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: by option: indwelling-system urinary symptoms; instillation-course irritation; Anktiva rides BCG's ledger; pembrolizumab brings the systemic immune ledger to a…
Newly diagnosed.patient: When BCG has failed but the tumor is still shallow: four newer bladder-keeping options exist, the best clearing the cancer in about eight of ten patients at first check - real progress, measured so far by response rather than long-term survival, and the card says so.

Newly diagnosed.name: Radical cystectomy for BCG-unresponsive disease (the survival standard)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN-preferred definitive option for BCG-unresponsive high-risk NMIBC (secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: surgical series (teaching estimate flagged); the comparator logic verified by the approvals themselves
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: a major operation and a permanent plumbing change - the honest price of the survival standard
Newly diagnosed.patient: Removing the bladder: the definitive answer when BCG has failed - the strongest survival numbers on this menu, at the cost of a big operation and a new way of passing urine.

Newly diagnosed.name: Perioperative systemic therapy + radical cystectomy (the twice-rewritten standard)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN MIBC framework (secondhand); NIAGARA approved 2025-03; EV+P all-comers 2026-07 (the labeled card beside this one)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x3 (SWOG-8710, NIAGARA, CheckMate 274) - receipts verified; the 5-yr percentage flagged
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: chemotherapy or chemo-IO season, then the operation and the diversion - the heaviest sequenced load in this trainer
Newly diagnosed.patient: For tumors into the muscle: strong medicine around a bladder-removing operation - the modern combinations cut recurrence substantially, and this road carries the field's deepest evidence.
drugs: Perioperative regimen (ddMVAC/GC +/- durvalumab; EV+P per the labeled card) -> cystectomy

Newly diagnosed.name: Perioperative EV + pembrolizumab (the 2026 rewrite - approved, conference-stage, labeled)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: FDA-approved 2026-07-10 for all cystectomy candidates (secondhand) - the newest perioperative standard, cited at conference grade
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized, CONFERENCE-STAGE (ESMO 2025 LBA; PubMed primary pending) - labeled until the paper lands
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the EV ledger (neuropathy, skin including the SJS/TEN warning, hyperglycemia/DKA) plus the immune ledger, wrapped around an operation - read the baseline befor…
Newly diagnosed.patient: The newest option around bladder-removal surgery: the antibody-plus-immunotherapy pair, freshly approved for everyone facing this operation - with results so new they exist as conference presentations, which is exactly what this card's label says.

Newly diagnosed.name: Trimodality bladder preservation (selected patients - the same-survival road)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN option for selected MIBC (secondhand); the selection criteria carried verbatim
Newly diagnosed.evidence: propensity-matched multi-institutional comparison (Zlotta) - no RCT exists, said plainly
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: radiation's bladder-and-bowel ledger plus radiosensitizing chemo - traded against the operation and the diversion; the kept bladder must still behave
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the right tumor, keeping the bladder: deep scraping plus radiation-with-chemo matched surgery's survival in the best modern comparison - the fine print is the selection (one tumor, the right size, a bladder worth keeping) and the check-up calendar that comes with it.
drugs: Maximal TURBT + chemoradiation (salvage cystectomy standing by)

Newly diagnosed.name: Enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab (EV-302 - the metastatic rewrite)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the 1L standard (PDQ lists it first; NCCN secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - OS HR 0.47 (NEJM 2024, PMID re-verified)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the EV ledger (neuropathy dose-modified early, skin watched to the SJS/TEN level, glucose checked) plus the immune ledger - gentler than chemo in aggregate (55…
Newly diagnosed.patient: For spread disease: the antibody-plus-immunotherapy pair nearly doubled median survival over chemotherapy - the clearest first-choice on this menu, and it does not require the kidney-and-fitness checklist chemotherapy does.

Newly diagnosed.name: Platinum + gemcitabine + nivolumab (CheckMate 901 - where EV+P cannot go)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: cisplatin-eligible alternative (NCCN secondhand); avelumab maintenance inside the platinum pathway (JAVELIN)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 (CheckMate 901; JAVELIN Bladder 100) - OS met in both
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: platinum's ledger (kidneys, ears, counts, nausea) plus the immune ledger - the road for those whose neuropathy or eyes rule the ADC out
Newly diagnosed.patient: The chemotherapy road, now with immunotherapy built in: for fit patients who cannot take the newer antibody pair - real survival benefit, and about one in five get deep responses lasting years.
drugs: Gemcitabine-cisplatin + nivolumab (avelumab maintenance where chemo ran alone)

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; hematuria and obstruction care are the craft
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining cancer-directed treatment is a real choice - with a team whose craft includes the bleeding and blockage problems this disease can cause.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Erdafitinib (THOR - the FGFR ticket)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: FDA-approved for FGFR3-altered post-systemic disease (2024-01, secondhand)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: hyperphosphatemia (managed by protocol), nail and skin changes, and the central serous retinopathy watch - eye exams are part of the prescription
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: If the tumor carries the FGFR gene change: a daily tablet beat chemotherapy on survival itself - the targeted door this disease's gene panel exists to find.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Taxane chemotherapy (the bar, measured live)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: randomized control-arm measurement (THOR) - the live bar
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: cytopenias, neuropathy, fatigue - the familiar taxane season
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The standard chemotherapy for this stage: modest, real, and honestly the yardstick the newer options are measured against.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Sacituzumab govitecan (the withdrawal - kept as the ledger's teaching card)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: WITHDRAWN from this indication 2024-10 (voluntary, with FDA) - not an option; a lesson
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: accelerated (phase 2 ORR) -> confirmatory phase 3 NEGATIVE with excess toxicity deaths -> withdrawn
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the withdrawal's stated reason includes the toxicity: neutropenic complications drove excess early deaths in the confirmatory trial
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A drug that used to be on this menu and no longer is: its provisional approval was withdrawn after the proving trial failed and showed extra harm - kept on this screen because knowing why options leave is part of trusting the ones that stay.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: none from therapy; hematuria and obstruction care remain the craft
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort after several lines is a real road, chosen with the true numbers on the table.

refs.label: NCI PDQ: Bladder Cancer Treatment (HP, updated 2025-05-02, loaded live 2026-08) - NMIBC/MIBC/metastatic framework; lists EV+P first in metastatic disease; smoking attribution framing

NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bladder Cancer V3.2026 (per search snippet; JNCCN reprint of V1.2026 in JNCCN 2026;24(5)); NCCN patient guideline 2026 edition. nccn.org 403 - ALL SECONDHAND, confirm versions on-site

Balar et al. KEYNOTE-057 cohort A: pembrolizumab in BCG-unresponsive CIS - CR 41% (39/96) at 3 months. Lancet Oncol 2021 (PMID 34051177, verified; cohort B papillary PMID 38740030). FDA 2020-01 (date secondhand)

Boorjian et al. Nadofaragene firadenovec (rAd-IFNa/Syn3) in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC - CIS cohort CR 53.4% (55/103) within 3 months; 45.5% of responders holding at 12 months. Lancet Oncol 2020 (PMID 33253641, verified; NCT02773849). FDA 2022-12 (secondhand)

Chamie et al. QUILT-3.032: nogapendekin alfa inbakicept (Anktiva) + BCG, BCG-unresponsive CIS - CR 71% (58/82), median duration 26.6 months; label basis (77 pts) CR 62%. NEJM Evid 2023 (PMID 38320011, verified). FDA 2024-04-22 (secondhand)

Daneshmand et al. SunRISe-1: TAR-200 (gemcitabine intravesical system) in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC - cohort 2 (CIS) CR 82.4% (CI 72.6-89.8), median DOR 25.8 months; papillary cohort 12-mo DFS 70.2%; grade >=3 TRAE 12.9%. JCO 2025 (PMID 40737582, verified; NCT04640623). FDA approved as INLEXZO 2025-09-09 (secondhand) - the first intravesical drug-releasing system

Grossman et al. SWOG-8710: neoadjuvant MVAC + cystectomy vs cystectomy - median OS 77 vs 46 months (P=0.06, the two-sided test that changed practice anyway); pT0 38% vs 15%. NEJM 2003;349:859-66 (PMID 12944571, verified)

Powles et al. NIAGARA: perioperative durvalumab + neoadjuvant GC (cisplatin-eligible MIBC) - 24-mo EFS 67.8% vs 59.8% (HR 0.68, p<0.001); 24-mo OS 82.2% vs 75.2% (HR 0.75, p=0.01); n=1,063. NEJM 2024;391:1773-86 (PMID 39282910, verified; NCT03732677). FDA 2025-03-28 (secondhand)

KEYNOTE-905/EV-303 (ESMO 2025 LBA2, Ann Oncol suppl): perioperative EV + pembrolizumab vs surgery alone, cisplatin-ineligible MIBC - EFS NR vs 15.7 months (HR 0.40), OS NR vs 41.7 (HR 0.50), pCR 57.1% vs 8.6%. CONFERENCE-STAGE: no peer-reviewed primary on PubMed as of 2026-08 - the card stays labeled until the paper lands (confirm via registry)

FDA 2026-07-10: pembrolizumab (+/- berahyaluronidase alfa) + enfortumab vedotin approved as neoadjuvant->adjuvant treatment for ALL MIBC cystectomy candidates (fda.gov announcement; exact label wording confirm via registry) - the second perioperative rewrite in eighteen months; carried beside NIAGARA, not instead of it

Bajorin et al. CheckMate 274: adjuvant nivolumab after radical surgery (high-risk MIUC) - median DFS 20.8 vs 10.8 months (HR 0.70, p<0.001); PD-L1>=1% HR 0.55. NEJM 2021;384:2102-14 (PMID 34077643, verified)

CheckMate 274 5-year update: DFS HR 0.74 holds; median OS 75.0 vs 50.1 months, HR 0.83 (CI 0.67-1.02) - OS NOT statistically significant, carried verbatim; benefit concentrated in ctDNA-positive patients (ctDNA-undetectable median DFS 52.1 vs 5.0 detectable). The honest adjuvant ledger: DFS real, OS unproven, ctDNA the live question (MODERN). Ann Oncol 2025 (PMID 41110694, verified)

Zlotta et al. Trimodality therapy vs radical cystectomy (propensity-matched, multi-institutional, SELECTED patients) - 5-yr metastasis-free survival 74-75% both arms (no difference); CSS/DFS no difference; OS favored TMT (HR 0.70-0.75). The same-survival receipt behind the deliberate tie. Lancet Oncol 2023 (PMID 37187202, verified)

Powles et al. EV-302/KEYNOTE-A39: enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab vs platinum chemo, 1L mUC - OS 31.5 vs 16.1 months (HR 0.47, p<0.001), PFS 12.5 vs 6.3 (HR 0.45); grade >=3 TRAE 55.9% vs 69.5%; n=886. NEJM 2024;390:875-88 (PMID 38446675 - the registry's earlier IMPOSTOR-PMID TRAP, re-checked and RE-PASSED this sweep; NCT04223856). Platinum-eligibility agnostic

van der Heijden et al. CheckMate 901: nivolumab + gemcitabine-cisplatin vs GC (cisplatin-eligible 1L) - OS 21.7 vs 18.9 (HR 0.78, p=0.02); ORR 57.6%, CR 21.7% with median CR duration 37.1 months. NEJM 2023;389:1778-89 (PMID 37870949, verified)

Powles et al. JAVELIN Bladder 100: avelumab switch-maintenance after non-progression on 1L platinum - OS 21.4 vs 14.3 months (HR 0.69, p=0.001). Taught INSIDE the platinum pathway post-EV-302, not as co-equal 1L. NEJM 2020;383:1218-30 (PMID 32945632, verified)

Loriot et al. THOR: erdafitinib vs chemotherapy (FGFR3/2-altered mUC post-anti-PD-(L)1) - OS 12.1 vs 7.8 months (HR 0.64, p=0.005), PFS 5.6 vs 2.7; the 7.8 control arm doubles as this trainer's live later-line chemo bar. NEJM 2023 (PMID 37870920, verified). Full FDA approval 2024-01 (secondhand)

Sacituzumab govitecan urothelial indication: accelerated approval (2021-04, TROPHY-U-01) VOLUNTARILY WITHDRAWN, announced 2024-10-18 (Gilead, in consultation with FDA), after confirmatory TROPiCS-04 missed its primary OS endpoint with more early deaths from adverse events (neutropenic complications/infections) vs chemotherapy. Other indications unaffected. The evidence-reversal card's receipt (sponsor statement; ORR figure on the card is a flagged teaching estimate - confirm via registry)

Galsky et al. Consensus definition of cisplatin ineligibility (any one: ECOG >=2, CrCl <60, grade >=2 hearing loss, grade >=2 neuropathy, NYHA >=III). Lancet Oncol 2011 (PMID 21376284, verified as citation; criteria thresholds confirm via full text)

BCG shortage: TICE BCG remains on allocation (ASHP shortage list); manufacturing expansion targeted to relieve meaningfully late 2026/2027; gem/docetaxel intravesical the named BCG-sparing alternative. Secondhand but multi-source-consistent (ASHP/Merck/BCAN) - re-check each refresh

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

MODERN / Alliance A032103 (NCT05987241): ctDNA-branched adjuvant therapy post-cystectomy - ctDNA+ -> nivolumab vs nivo+relatlimab; ctDNA- -> nivolumab vs surveillance; n=992, ~500 US sites, ECOG 0-2 - registry-verified 2026-08 (endpoint split web-verified; one confirmatory registry pull at refresh)

AstraZeneca (NCT07720284): adjuvant Dato-DXd + rilvegostomig vs SOC adjuvant IO, high-risk MIBC/MIUC post-R0 resection, phase 3, n=915, 160 sites, opened 2026-07 - registry-verified 2026-08 (primary-endpoint text pending a registry pull - flagged)
ARCHER / NRG (NCT07097142): adaptive hypofractionated chemoradiation for MIBC T2-T3a preservation candidates, phase 3, 211 sites - registry-verified 2026-08

MoonRISe-2 (NCT06919965): TAR-210 (erdafitinib intravesical system) vs intravesical chemo, HR-NMIBC post-BCG with susceptible FGFR alterations, phase 3, 112 sites - registry-verified 2026-08. MoonRISe-1 (NCT06319820, intermediate-risk): overall RECRUITING but US sites effectively closed - the registry-honest caveat

FORAGER-2 (NCT07218380): vepugratinib (LOXO-435, FGFR3-selective) + EV+P vs placebo + EV+P, untreated la/mUC with FGFR3 alteration, phase 3 double-blind, 289 sites, PFS-BICR primary - registry-verified 2026-08. No classic chemo-comparator 1L phase 3 recruits with US sites today

TROPION-Urothelial03 (NCT07129993): Dato-DXd + platinum vs gemcitabine-platinum after progression on 1L EV+P, phase 2/3, n=630, US sites recruiting - registry-verified 2026-08.
